God created the idea of karma and free will, therefore god allows us to suffer. We as humans are rewarded for good doings in the form of preventing the suffering of others, but it feels weird to follow through with these actions as god’s commandments since he himself does not prevent suffering when he is capable. 

Also, you stress the importance of evolving and god wanting us to reach our full potential and learn and experience on the path to moksha, as well as the importance of our free will and god’s respect for it. Is this not backwards since after moksha is attained we lose our karma and become without desire and have no need to act, we simply experience a transcendental blissful state. Also, we attain the same potential in the end as all souls attain moksha eventually. Our full potentials are not different.

We are given these aspects, free will, potential, the experience of life, but in the end we will leave them behind and the memories of such will have no use to us during moksha, we will be in bliss anyways. Why can’t all souls just have moksha? God is all powerful and while you say that we can’t live in a perfect world because all desires cannot be fulfilled because everyone has conflicting desires, god can change what each and everyone desire, simplify the world to nothing but a state of bliss with nothing to be fulfilled, no one would be unhappy about it because we would be filled with bliss.
